s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden onset of severe, episodic, unilateral facial pain with trigeminal nerve distribution, triggered by specific movements
salient_findings: Severe pain on the left side of the face
Pain localized to the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve
Allodynia to cold air and hypersensitivity to touch in the affected area
key_facts: 36-year-old woman
Persistent severe pain on the left side of her face
Pain started after receiving the third dose of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine
Episodic sharp, electric-shock–like pain
Pain triggered by jaw movement during eating or tooth brushing
Attacks lasted 4–5 seconds
Pain reached 10/10 on a numeric pain scale
Distorted sensations in the V2 region during attacks
Sensory testing was otherwise normal
No other neurological deficits
No relevant past medical or family history
Routine laboratory tests, including D-dimer, were normal
RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2 and other infections was negative
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the head showed no abnormalities

shortlist.label: Trigeminal Neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Classic presentation of episodic, sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the trigeminal nerve distribution, triggered by jaw movement

shortlist.label: Glossopharyngeal Neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to trigeminal neuralgia, but less common, and the pain is typically in the throat or tongue

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Demyelinating disease that can cause facial pain, although less typical than other symptoms

shortlist.label: Tolosa-Hunt Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Rare condition causing unilateral facial pain, often accompanied by other symptoms like diplopia or ptosis

shortlist.label: Raeder Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Rare condition with facial pain, often accompanied by other symptoms like miosis or ptosis, and typically related to a lesion in the middle cranial fossa
